Scratch has entered its 3.0 era, and because of this, mobile devices are supported! But since mobile devices have no keyboard, many projects are incompatible with them. This studio is to collect projects that are fully usable on mobile devices. This studio has a partner studio for resources at https://scratch.mit.edu/studios/5868311/ . If you want to become a curator, give a link to one of your mobile-friendly projects first.\
\
✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧\
\
◉ What is mobile-friendliness?\
▶︎ Mobile-friendliness is a state where a project can be navigated and used by a person on a mobile device just as well as by a person on a computer. For more info, see https://scratch.mit.edu/projects/270693321/\
\
◉ What projects can go here?\
► Any project that has a control scheme that is fully usable with touchscreen controls can be added to this studio. It's fine if the project allows keyboard input as well. (Please don't suggest or add projects that have no interaction, though.) Remixes are allowed. For inspiration, look at some of the projects here!\
\
◉ What are the rules?\
► This studio is for the collection and discussion of mobile-friendly projects, and shouldn't be used for other things. Please don't remove and re-add your projects, and keep this studio a friendly place for all who may visit. Curators should add not only projects suggested in the comments, but also add any mobile-friendly projects they come across elsewhere. Do not ask for managers and curators to add your featured project, always copy the project link instead.\
\
◉ Can I curate?\
► If you've made a project that is mobile-friendly and you suggest it in the comments asking to curate, then a manager should invite you. Please don't just ask to curate without a mobile-friendly project. Curators will get promoted to managers if they add projects frequently.\
\
◉ How can I make my project mobile-friendly?\
► There are many ways! Have a look at the tips below, ask questions about it here, or check the official Mobile-Friendly Resources studio at https://scratch.mit.edu/studios/5868311/\
\
◉ I have other questions!\
► If you have any other questions about mobile-friendliness or this studio, then feel free to ask them in the comments!\
\
✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧\
\
▶︎ Mobile-Friendly Project Tips ◀︎\
◉ Make sure that all keyboard operations can be done with the mouse as well!\
◉ You can't change the mouse-pointer's position without having the mouse-pointer down on mobile devices.\
◉ The only way to input text on mobile is in 'ask [] and wait' blocks.\
◉ Try using swipe controls if you don't want lots of buttons. - @TheBurlyCoconut\
◉ Try programming different modes for different platforms with the mobile mode having modified controls. - @petra8\
◉ Remember that you can't tap 2 buttons at once on mobile! This makes simultaneous multiplayer games impossible to play. Make buttons that combine multiple inputs. - @happybird123\
◉ Clicker games can be easily be played on mobile since it is just clicking to upgrade. - @Tyhond-Team-Ufaro\
◉ Avoid using 'when this sprite clicked' for buttons in games, as you can't hold it down! Use 'if <<touching [mouse-pointer v] ?> and <mouse down?>> then' instead. - @happybird123\
◉ If you want to make a platformer, have there be 2 jump buttons that also move horizontally, as it's much easier to control. - @happybird123\
◉ Turbo Mode is difficult to activate on phones, so avoid making projects reliant on it.\
◉ An easy way to check if something is being tapped: use the blocks 'if <<touching [mouse-pointer v] ?> and <mouse down?>> then' - @CoolPenguin10\
◉ Some projects can't be loaded on mobile because too much is loaded at once or there's a lot of data in your project. Try to optimize the best you can by avoiding vector graphics and long songs.\
◉ Projects can crash if there are too many costumes in use, so try to limit the amount of costumes. - @SuperSean12\
◉ Make on-screen buttons transparent if it's possible for objects to go underneath them. - @aiden_20121\
\
Anyone can suggest a tip to be added to this description!\
\
✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧✧\
\

\
To stop this, we need to spread the message (please don't advertise on random people's profile, but make several studios and projects relevant to this) that we should report users who do this and that people generally shouldn't do it. \

I've recently seen two users who left Scratch because of their projects getting false-reported. If you're a false-reporter, I won't even hesitate to say that you are a HORRIBLE PERSON who is just jealous of famous and innocent Scratchers who make innocent projects. \

We all spent years of our lives working towards this moment, to finally graduation high school or earn a degree, and then when the time has finally come, we are being denied the chance to be honored in the traditional way and with our friends and family there to support us. Many in the past got the opportunity, but those graduating this year did not.\
\
Lets all come together to honor and celebrate our fellow graduating Scratchers of the Class of 2020!\
\
A virtual graduation ceremony will be taking place on June 10, 2020.\
\
It will not be live, but rather any related Scratch projects that will be a part of it, will be shared on that date.\
----------------------------------------\
Only projects related to the graduating class of 2020 and/or are honoring/celebrating a scratcher who is graduating this year (which can be yourself, if your graduating this year) are allowed in this studio.\
\
If you are not a curator and have a project you'd like added, comment a link and a curator will add it.\
\
If you are graduating this year and/or receiving a degree, will be participating in the graduation ceremony, and are not a studio curator, but would like to be, ask in the comments and @miles854 will invite you.\
\
Note: The only studio managers are the studio owner and graduation ceremony commencment speakers.\
-----------------------------------------Graduation Event Information-\
\
The Scratch Graduation Ceremony took place on June 10, 2020. \
\
All of the Scratchers taking part in the ceremony remixed a project which included providing their OC wearing a cap and gown. Each OC was put into a project featuring an image of a virtual graduation ceremonies audience.\
That project is at:\
https://scratch.mit.edu/projects/396672862/\
\
Each of the Scratchers taking part in the ceremony are given a special diploma, signed by @miles854 (who put together the virtual ceremony) and the commencment speakers. You can remix it and add your username. The diploma is at https://scratch.mit.edu/projects/396805362/\
\
Also on June 10, 2020, a project featuring a diploma for this virtual Scratch graduation will be shared. It will be \signed\" by @miles854 (who planned/set up this graduation) and the commencment speakers.\

Hey everybody! Today I have an announcement to make.\
\
Stop fighting for fame! I just don't get it. Why do so many Scratchers think they HAVE to be FAMOUS? Scratch is a place to learn the basic principles of coding, such as variables, lists, functions, etc. It isn't a place to get famous. If you want to get famous, actually LEARN from Scratch, then move on to something more advanced such as Roblox, Unity, Unreal Engine, or Snap! If you just want to learn Scratch in your free time for fun or just for the sake of knowing another language, that's fine! Remember, knowledge IS power! Scratch is about learning and having fun! A good way to learn if your just starting out is to watch tutorials or look in other Scratcher's projects and try to understand what the code is doing. (Tutorial tip: Watch tutorials where someone actually explains how the code works. If they are just giving you all the code and not explaining it at all, that's completely pointless because you don't learn anything from it.) It's ok to WANT to be famous on Scratch, it's just not okay to let that take away from your fun and learning. Make projects that YOU want to make, not projects that you know OTHERS will want to see.\
\
